description: Building E.V.A. for the 'Trend Detective!' challenge—a climate intelligence platform using stats on NASA data. Our team is skilled in software, AI, and UX. We seek members with skills in Earth/data science, front-end, or business storytelling to turn complex data into an impactful, award-winning project. Join us!
summary:
EVA Classroom brings NASA’s public data closer to real-world classrooms, transforming complex datasets into a playful and interactive climate investigation experience.

Through a digital globe, charts, and historical time series, teachers and students explore real temperature and precipitation data, compare regions and time periods, and investigate changes across the planet. EVA, the virtual assistant, helps interpret observations and develop hypotheses, encouraging critical thinking without presenting correlations as proven causes. The MVP also features interactive quizzes to encourage classroom participation.

The solution uses an automated process for data collection, processing, and updates, including invalid record filtering, unit standardization, and the analysis of historical trends and variations. This connects scientific information with accessible tools for education.

The project has been presented to school administrators from both a public school and a private educational institution, who expressed interest in evaluating a pilot program. With the MVP now available, Team EVA aims to empower a generation capable of understanding climate change, asking meaningful questions, and making evidence-based decisions.
details:
EVA Classroom (Earth Variance Analytics) turns environmental data into an interactive learning experience. Teachers and students explore temperature, rainfall and satellite observations through a 3D globe, historical charts and a timeline covering 1981–2025.

The platform uses MERRA-2, AIRS/Aqua and Copernicus/ESA Sentinel-5P data distributed through NASA. Python and Node.js scripts extract scientific files, filter invalid observations, standardize units and organize measurements by location and period in JSON. Linear regression across annual observations summarizes trends, while comparisons against a 1981–2010 baseline highlight variations. Country colors represent available samples, not national averages.

Google Gemini receives calculated results and context through a server-side API to explain patterns, suggest hypotheses and propose classroom investigations. Application code performs the calculations; AI supports interpretation without treating possible causes as proven facts.

Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, Python and Node.js, the project uses Vercel and GitHub. Its bilingual interface, expressive mascot and simulated classroom quiz make scientific data approachable. Designed for desktop, mobile and classroom projection, EVA aims to strengthen data literacy, scientific curiosity and environmental awareness. Two education leaders expressed interest in evaluating a pilot.
